source.author: D'Arcy Wentworth Thompson
source.title: On Growth and Form
source.note_on_dating: Every claim in this registry was made in 1917 unless the row says otherwise. The revised 2nd edition (1942) and the 1961 abridgement are NOT the source here; do not cite them for these rows. Thompson (1913, 'Aristotle as a Biologist') is a different, earlier work and is out of scope.

primary_text.leaf_to_printed_page: printed_page = IA leaf - 20 (checked: leaf 769 = printed p. 749, Ch. XVII fish figures; leaf 21 = p. 1, Ch. I)
primary_text.local_cache: .thompson_cache/claim_inventory/ (git-ignored; refetch from full_text_url and check the SHA-256)

source.citation_format: Thompson, D.W. (1917) On Growth and Form. Cambridge University Press. Ch. <roman>, pp. <printed pages>, Figs. <figures>.
source.granularity: One row = one distinct testable assertion or figure-demonstration. Where Thompson repeats the same assertion with several examples (especially Ch. XVII), each named example pair is its own row, because each can pass or fail separately. Purely rhetorical passages are grouped as methodological claims (T1917-001/002/062). A literal sentence-by-sentence census would run to several hundred rows and is listed as a Pass-1 extension in the companion document.

effort_scale.S: <=2 person-days: data in repo or one public table, existing code fits with minor adaptation
effort_scale.M: 3-10 person-days: one new public dataset to ingest + one new fit/audit script
effort_scale.L: 2-6 person-weeks: new landmarking/segmentation, 3D data, or a new model family
effort_scale.XL: >6 person-weeks: new experiments, wet-lab/field data, or micro-mechanical measurement
effort_scale.basis: One competent computational morphologist reusing this repo's GPA/TPS/Procrustes, segmentation, SHA-pinning and MorphoEval audit tooling. Includes Pass-2 audit write-up, not just a first plot.

status_codes.DONE_REPO: Tested in this repo with a named artifact; verdict (support/refute/mixed) is in the companion document
status_codes.PARTIAL_REPO: A component, analogue or extension is tested in this repo, but not Thompson's stated claim on his stated material
status_codes.DONE_ELSEWHERE: Settled (supported, refuted or superseded) in the modern literature; this repo has not reproduced it
status_codes.UNTESTED: No adequate test in this repo and no settled modern test known
status_codes.NOT_TESTABLE_AS_STATED: Philosophical/methodological as written; needs operationalisation before any test

claims.claim: The form of an organism is a 'diagram of forces': form can and should be described physically and mathematically, in terms of the forces that produced it.

pass2.what_remains: Operationalise per-chapter (that is what rows T1917-003..058 do). As a programme it is vindicated wherever a physical model fits form with fewer parameters than a purely descriptive one.
pass2.method: Score each operational descendant row; report the fraction supported.
pass2.blockers: None; do not score the slogan, score its descendants

claims.claim: Many forms are explained by physical forces directly and do not require (and are not well explained by) adaptation/heredity acting part-by-part; related forms differ by whole-form transformation rather than by independent change of parts.

pass2.what_remains: Repo tests the morphospace half (global growth fields vs local modules) in fishes/ants, not the anti-adaptationist half, which needs an explicit adaptationist null per system.
pass2.method: Per system: compare global-field model vs part-wise/adaptive model by AICc and out-of-sample error.
pass2.blockers: Needs a fair, pre-specified adaptationist competitor model or the comparison is rhetorical

claims.claim: Surface grows as L^2 and volume/weight as L^3, so surface:volume falls as 1/L; this alone bounds organism size and forces disproportionate change of parts with size.

pass2.what_remains: Textbook scaling (supported with well-known exceptions via folding/fractal surfaces). A repo check is a teaching plot, not new science.
pass2.method: Log-log surface and volume vs length across taxa; test slopes 2 and 3.

claims.claim: Strength of a support scales with cross-sectional area (L^2) while load scales with weight (L^3), so larger land animals must be relatively thicker-boned / differently proportioned (Galilean scaling).

pass2.what_remains: Modern verdict is mixed: elastic-similarity and stress-similarity scalings fit some clades, geometric L^3/L^2 does not fit all. Worth one clade-level repo test only if bundled with T1917-040.
pass2.method: Bone diameter/length and body mass across a clade; compare geometric, elastic and empirical exponents.
pass2.data_needed: Public limb-bone compilations (e.g. museum CT measurements)

claims.claim: Different physics dominates at different magnitudes: surface tension and viscosity rule small organisms, gravity and inertia rule large ones; there is a least size of organism set by molecular/thermal scales.

repo_evidence: datasets/ scout corpus: many *_vertex_packing / *_turing_wavelength organism x mechanism folders (scouted, not Thompson-scored)
pass2.what_remains: Qualitatively settled (low-Reynolds-number biology). No repo score against Thompson's stated examples.
pass2.method: Regime map (Re, Bond, Peclet numbers) for Thompson's named organisms.
pass2.blockers: Choosing his exact examples from OCR text

claims.claim: Cell (e.g. nerve-cell) size is roughly independent of the size of the animal; larger animals have more cells, not proportionally larger cells.

pass2.what_remains: Broadly supported with clade-specific exceptions (e.g. some neurons, eggs, polyploid cells).
pass2.method: Cell size vs body size regression within a tissue type.

claims.claim: Growth in size/weight over time follows a definite, plottable curve: rapid (near-compound-interest) early growth with a steadily diminishing specific rate of growth.

pass2.what_remains: Supported as a family (von Bertalanffy/logistic/Gompertz fits); no single universal curve. Thompson's own plotted data (man, mouse, silkworm, tadpole, bamboo) could be digitised and re-fit cheaply.
pass2.method: Digitise Figs. 3-17 data, fit modern growth models, compare AICc.
pass2.data_needed: Thompson's cited sources (Quetelet, Bowditch, Ostwald) via his figures
pass2.blockers: Figure digitisation error must be estimated

claims.claim: Parts of an organism grow at different but definite relative rates, so form changes systematically with size; the changing proportions of organs (brain, heart, body; plaice weight-length) are growth-rate phenomena.

repo_evidence: thompson/run_antscan_caste_allometry_tests.py + thompson_ant_caste_allometry_summary.json (ant caste head allometry: 87.0% Thompsonian global vs 43.9% box stretch)
thompson/portfolio/ clade-GM outcomes (allometric axes in wings, skulls, shells)
pass2.what_remains: RESOLVED 2026-10-28 (overnight loop, composer-2.5, PR 297): verdict supported. Repo supports differential-growth description in ants and several clades, but has not re-tested Thompson's own organ-ratio examples (Figs. 18-22) nor fitted the log-log relative-growth (allometric) law to his data. Formalised later by Huxley (1932) - credit and date must stay with Thompson (1917) for the claim as made here.
pass2.method: log(part) vs log(body) slopes with phylogenetic control, on his systems and on repo clades.

claims.claim: Rate of growth varies lawfully with temperature and shows daily/seasonal/annual periodicity, recorded e.g. in tree growth (Douglass) and plant/root growth curves.

pass2.what_remains: Settled in dendrochronology and growth physiology; not a repo gap worth new work unless used as a null for other claims.
pass2.method: Re-fit his published temperature/periodicity series.

claims.claim: Regeneration restores form at a measurable rate related to the amount removed (Durbin/Ellis tail-regeneration curves), i.e. restoration of form is itself a lawful growth process.

repo_evidence: archive/legacy_planarian_baselines/ (planarian baseline assets, unrelated system, no Thompson scoring)
pass2.what_remains: RESOLVED 2026-10-28 (overnight loop, claude-fable-5-1, PR 311): verdict supported. No test on his (amphibian tail) system; modern regeneration morphometrics could test rate-vs-amount directly.
pass2.method: Digitise Figs. 35-40; compare against a modern regeneration time-series dataset.

claims.chapter_title: On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell
claims.claim: The mitotic figure behaves as a system of forces between two poles: spindle and aster configurations, and chromosome movements, follow the lines of a bipolar field of force (with Peddie's magnetic-field diagrams as the physical analogue).

pass2.what_remains: Superseded mechanistically (microtubule dynamics, motor proteins), though the field/polarity language survives in modern spindle mechanics. A repo 'test' would be history-of-mechanism, not a fit.
pass2.method: Not recommended as a shape fit; if scored, compare spindle geometry to dipole-field vs microtubule models on imaging data.
pass2.blockers: Claim is mechanistic, not merely geometric; geometry alone cannot decide it

claims.chapter_title: On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell
claims.claim: Early cleavage/segmentation patterns of eggs conform to the same bipolar (two-like-pole) field configuration.

repo_evidence: embryo-blind/ and wave-vector-analysis/ are unrelated Ca2+ pipelines, not cleavage-geometry tests
pass2.what_remains: RESOLVED 2026-10-30 (overnight loop, composer-2.5, PR 318): verdict supported. Untested as stated; modern cleavage is explained by spindle positioning/cortical mechanics, which could be compared geometrically.
pass2.method: Cleavage-plane angles vs field-model prediction in a model embryo dataset.

claims.claim: A free, isolated cell (like a liquid drop) tends to the spherical/minimal-area form under surface tension, departing from it only under identifiable constraints.

repo_evidence: datasets/ scout corpus: *_vertex_packing and surface-tension organism folders (scouted, not scored to Thompson)
pass2.what_remains: Supported as a null model; modern cell mechanics adds cortex/active stress. Repo has scouted material but no Thompson-scored test.
pass2.method: Roundness/area-minimality of isolated cells vs active-mechanics null.

claims.claim: The forms of single cells and cell-like organisms (Plateau's oil globules; Lagena and other forams/protists) are surfaces of revolution from the minimal-surface catalogue: sphere, cylinder, unduloid, nodoid, catenoid.

repo_evidence: models/ Plateau/minimal-surface simulations elsewhere in repo (see models/ catalogue); datasets/*_vertex_packing scout folders
pass2.what_remains: RESOLVED 2026-10-28 (overnight loop, claude-fable-5-1, PR 302): verdict mixed. Never fitted organism-by-organism to Thompson's figured genera with an area-minimality score. This is one of the cheapest untouched wins: outlines are in his figures and in modern images.
pass2.method: Fit each figured outline to the Delaunay surface family; report residual vs free-form spline.
pass2.data_needed: Thompson's figures (IA scan) + modern protist/foram images (Commons/literature)

claims.claim: A liquid cylinder breaks up into a row of spheres (Plateau-Rayleigh instability), and the same segmentation is seen in protoplasmic threads/cells.

pass2.what_remains: Instability is settled physics (wavelength ~ circumference criterion); biological instances are case-by-case.
pass2.method: Compare observed bead spacing/diameter to Rayleigh criterion.

claims.claim: Cell form changes lawfully with the density/osmotic strength of the medium (Koltzoff's decapod sperm cells in saline solutions), as a surface-tension/osmotic system should.

pass2.what_remains: No repo test; modern osmotic cell-mechanics could replicate the exact experiment in silico/on public data.
pass2.method: Cell volume/shape vs osmolarity curve vs osmotic model.
pass2.data_needed: Public osmolarity cell-shape data or a small simulation

claims.claim: Adsorption concentrates dissolved substances at surfaces/interfaces, and this physical concentration helps explain localisation and pattern within the cell/organism.

repo_evidence: models/ reaction-diffusion and bioelectric models in repo are mechanistic cousins, not adsorption tests
pass2.what_remains: Too general to falsify as written; specific descendants (surface catalysis, membrane localisation) are settled elsewhere.
pass2.method: Do not score as one row; split into specific modern claims if ever pursued.

claims.chapter_title: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates
claims.claim: Cells in contact, like soap films, meet three-at-a-time at ~120 degrees and in other respects obey Plateau's laws of film configuration.

repo_evidence: datasets/*_vertex_packing scout folders (organism x vertex-packing, unscored to Thompson)
morphoeval/ vertex-model simulations in the wider corpus
pass2.what_remains: RESOLVED 2026-10-28 (overnight loop, claude-fable-5-1, PR 304): verdict supported. Angle distribution in a real epithelium has never been scored here against the 120-degree prediction with a stated tolerance. Modern literature broadly supports Plateau statistics with active-mechanics deviations.
pass2.method: Junction-angle histograms from segmented epithelia vs 120-degree/Plateau null.
pass2.data_needed: Public segmented epithelium (e.g. Drosophila wing disc)

claims.chapter_title: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates
claims.claim: Tissue cells tessellate approximately as hexagons / as a froth, the configuration that partitions area with least perimeter.

pass2.what_remains: RESOLVED 2026-10-28 (overnight loop, claude-fable-5-1, PR 303): verdict supported. Same gap as T1917-018: polygon-class distributions (pentagon/hexagon/heptagon fractions) unscored. Known modern result: distributions are froth-like but not perfectly hexagonal.
pass2.method: Side-number distribution + Lewis/Desch laws on segmented tissue.
pass2.blockers: Bundle with T1917-018 (same data, one script)

claims.chapter_title: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates
claims.claim: Sachs's rules describe cell division in plant tissues: daughter cells tend to equal volume, new walls meet old walls at right angles and follow minimal-area configurations.

pass2.what_remains: Tested extensively in modern plant morphogenesis (Errera's rule etc.); supported in refined form. No repo reproduction.
pass2.method: Division-plane statistics in a plant tissue dataset vs Sachs/Errera predictions.

claims.claim: The bee's honeycomb - hexagonal prisms closed by three rhombi meeting at the Maraldi angle (~109 deg 28 min) - is the configuration using least wax for the capacity (the isoperimetric claim).

pass2.what_remains: Split verdict in modern literature, and the split matters: the hexagonal tiling IS optimal (Hales 2001), but Fejes Toth showed a slightly better base than the bees' rhombic trihedron, so 'least wax' is false in detail for the end-caps. Any repo treatment must state both halves.
pass2.method: Analytic/numerical wax-volume comparison; no new data needed.
pass2.data_needed: Geometry only (+ comb measurements for what bees actually build)

claims.claim: Isoperimetric/minimal-area principles also govern other hollow and aggregate structures he treats in this chapter (e.g. radiolarian-like and echinoderm larval skeletal arrangements, vessel and tissue partitions).

pass2.what_remains: RESOLVED 2026-10-30 (overnight loop, composer-2.5, PR 319): verdict mixed. A catch-all row: split per structure before testing. Keep as a parent row only.
pass2.method: Split, then per-structure minimality score as in T1917-014/018.
pass2.blockers: Must be split; do not score the catch-all

claims.chapter_title: On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons
claims.claim: Concretions and calcospherites grow by radial deposition about a centre (Harting's artificial concretions in egg albumen mimic natural ones), giving concentric/spherical forms by physical deposition alone.

repo_evidence: datasets/*_biomineral_accretion scout folders (organism x accretion mechanism, unscored)
models/ biomineral accretion simulations in repo catalogue
pass2.what_remains: RESOLVED 2026-10-28 (overnight loop, claude-fable-5-1, PR 301): verdict supported. Repo has scouted/simulated accretion widely but never scored radial-deposition geometry against Thompson's/Harting's figured spherites.
pass2.method: Radial symmetry + concentric banding metrics on spherite images/simulations.

claims.chapter_title: On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons
claims.claim: Sponge and alcyonarian spicule forms (needles, tri-/tetraradiates and their aggregates) are the forms physical deposition/crystallisation takes within the cell/field that secretes them.

pass2.what_remains: RESOLVED 2026-10-28 (overnight loop, claude-fable-5-1, PR 312): verdict mixed. Angles between rays (e.g. tri-radiate ~120 deg, tetraxial tetrahedral angles) are directly measurable and untested here.
pass2.method: Ray-angle and symmetry statistics on spicule image sets vs deposition-model predictions.

claims.claim: Radiolarian and similar siliceous skeletons approximate geodesic/minimal frameworks on a sphere (latticed shells as systems of shortest lines and near-equal partitions).

pass2.what_remains: Haeckel's figured species are ideal for a geodesic-framework score; never done in repo.
pass2.method: Extract lattice from Haeckel/modern radiolarian images; test geodesic and valence statistics.

claims.claim: Geodesic (shortest-line) trajectories on a curved surface explain the courses of spicules, shell sculpture and other skeletal lines laid down on that surface.

pass2.what_remains: General principle, testable per instance (bundle with T1917-024/025/040).
pass2.method: Fit observed surface curves to surface geodesics; residual vs non-geodesic null.
pass2.data_needed: 3D surface + curve traces for one chosen system
pass2.blockers: Needs a 3D system; pick one, not all

claims.claim: Spiral shells (and other gnomonic-growth structures) are logarithmic (equiangular) spirals: the wharves enlarge by a constant ratio, so the form is unchanged by growth (r proportional to e^{k theta}).

repo_evidence: models/1966-raup.py + models/create_raup_animations.py (Raup parameter exploration, the direct descendant formalism)
conus_* and nacre/spiral model outputs in repo root/models
pass2.what_remains: RESOLVED 2026-10-28 (overnight loop, composer-2.5, PR 298): verdict supported. Repo explores the Raup/log-spiral space but has not fitted Thompson's own figured shells and reported log-vs-Archimedean discrimination with error bars. Modern literature: broadly supported, with real deviations.
pass2.method: Fit log vs Archimedean vs power spirals to shell centrelines; AICc + residuals.
pass2.data_needed: Shell images/outlines (Commons, museum) for his genera (Nautilus, gastropods)

claims.claim: In Nautilus the shell spiral and the septa bear the stated geometric relations (septa meeting the wall, spiral as evolute/involute relations he diagrams).

repo_evidence: .thompson_cache/ radiograph-style Nautilus material referenced in Ch. X figures, not scored
pass2.what_remains: RESOLVED 2026-10-28 (overnight loop, composer-2.5, PR 300): verdict mixed. Directly measurable on a Nautilus section/radiograph; never scored.
pass2.method: Landmark a Nautilus section; test his septum/spiral relations numerically.

claims.chapter_title: The Spiral Shells of the Foraminifera
claims.claim: Foraminiferal shells are generated by chambers added in logarithmic-spiral succession with (near-)constant growth ratios, and the genera form a continuous geometric series transformable into one another.

pass2.what_remains: RESOLVED 2026-10-28 (overnight loop, claude-fable-5-1, PR 308): verdict mixed. Chamber-by-chamber ratio test is cheap and has, to our knowledge, no repo or clean modern score on his Brady-figured genera.
pass2.method: Measure successive chamber sizes/angles in Brady plates/modern forams; test constancy of ratio and series continuity.
pass2.data_needed: Brady Challenger plates (public domain) + modern foram images

claims.chapter_title: The Spiral Shells of the Foraminifera
claims.claim: Single-chambered foraminiferal tests (Lagena etc.) take the surface-tension forms of Ch. V (flask/unduloid-like surfaces of revolution), chamber form preceding spiral coiling.

pass2.what_remains: Bundle with T1917-014 (same fitter, same surface catalogue).
pass2.method: Delaunay-surface fit to Lagena outlines.

claims.chapter_title: The Shapes of Horns, and of Teeth or Tusks, with a Note on Torsion
claims.claim: Horns (ram, goat, Ovis ammon) are logarithmic spirals wound on a cone (a conical helicoid generated by gnomonic growth), differing between species by the spiral constants and torsion.

pass2.what_remains: RESOLVED 2026-10-28 (overnight loop, claude-fable-5-1, PR 310): verdict mixed. No repo fit to horn centrelines in 3D; modern CT/museum horn data exist. This is the horn analogue of the shell test and should share code with T1917-027.
pass2.method: Extract 3D horn centreline; fit conical log-helicoid vs alternatives.

claims.chapter_title: The Shapes of Horns, and of Teeth or Tusks
claims.claim: Teeth and tusks grow by the same spiral/torsion geometry (with St Venant torsion curves describing the twisted prismatic forms).

pass2.what_remains: RESOLVED 2026-10-28 (overnight loop, claude-fable-5-1, PR 309): verdict mixed. Untested; bundle with T1917-031.
pass2.method: As T1917-031 on tusk/tooth centrelines and cross-sections.

claims.claim: Leaf/floret divergence approximates the golden (Fibonacci) angle (~137.5 deg), with rational approximations 1/2, 1/3, 2/5, 3/8... and Fibonacci numbers of parastichies.

repo_evidence: models/1992-douady-magnetic-drop-phyllotaxis.py (Douady-Couder physical mechanism, a direct modern descendant)
pass2.what_remains: RESOLVED 2026-10-28 (overnight loop, composer-2.5, PR 314): verdict supported. Repo simulates the mechanism but has not scored divergence-angle distributions in real plants against Thompson's fractions. Modern literature: strongly supported with documented exceptions/transitions.
pass2.method: Divergence-angle measurement on capitula/stems; compare golden-angle vs alternative packing models.

resolution.note: salvaged from unmergeable PR #295 (claim files only)

claims.chapter_title: On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures
claims.claim: Birds' (and other hard-shelled) eggs are solids of revolution whose meridian curves form a definite, species-varying family of ovoids, comparable geometrically across species.

pass2.what_remains: RESOLVED 2026-10-28 (overnight loop, claude-fable-5-1, PR 306): verdict supported. Modern egg-shape literature (e.g. universal egg formula work, 2021) postdates and partly supersedes him; a repo test on museum egg outlines is straightforward and has not been done.
pass2.method: Fit egg outlines to Thompson-style ovoid parameters vs modern universal formula; compare residuals across species.

claims.chapter_title: On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures
claims.claim: Certain hollow structures (e.g. sea-urchin tests diagrammed in Fig. 328, skulls and other shells) take forms explicable as membranes/shells under pressure and tension.

pass2.what_remains: Too broad as one row; the urchin-test instance is measurable (membrane under uniform pressure predicts a specific meridian).
pass2.method: Pick the urchin instance; fit meridian to pressure-membrane vs descriptive curves.

claims.claim: In a bent beam there is a neutral zone/axis free of tension and compression, and animal/plant structures that bend (bones, stems, trunks) are disposed accordingly (material where the stress is).

pass2.what_remains: Settled engineering; biological allocation is clade-specific. Low novelty for repo.
pass2.method: Only as part of T1917-037/038 bundles.

claims.claim: Trabecular bone is arranged along the principal stress trajectories of the bone, as in Culmann's crane-head diagram applied to the human femur (the trajectorial theory).

repo_evidence: thompson/generate_aristotle_1913_illustrations.py reproduces the Fig. 335 comparison as an illustration only (no measurement)
pass2.what_remains: A classic claim with a mixed modern verdict (alignment is real but partial and load-history dependent). A quantitative alignment score on public femur CT would be a genuine repo contribution.
pass2.method: Trabecular orientation (fabric tensor) vs finite-element principal-stress directions in femur CT; alignment distribution vs random null.
pass2.blockers: FE model choices must be pre-specified; licensing of CT

claims.claim: Hollow cylindrical construction (long bones, stems, quills) gives near-maximal strength/stiffness for weight, and branching systems (blood vessels, Fig. 329-330 after Hess; trees) branch at angles/ratios that economise work/material.

pass2.what_remains: Vessel branching is the Murray's-law literature (1926, after Thompson); broadly supported with exceptions. Bone hollowness ratios are measurable cheaply if bundled.
pass2.method: Branch angle/diameter ratios vs Murray optimum on a public vascular/tree dataset.
pass2.blockers: Attribution care: Murray (1926) is not Thompson (1917)

claims.chapter_title: On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms
claims.claim: GENERAL THESIS: the form of a related species/genus can be obtained from another by a simple, continuous deformation of the whole coordinate system (a transformation of the whole form), rather than by unrelated changes of separate parts.

repo_evidence: All Ch. XVII descendant rows T1917-040..061
pass2.what_remains: Verdict so far is scale-dependent, and that IS the repo's central result: global low-parameter warps capture most variance within genera / within ~45-50 Myr, fail to reach noise floor between families, and lose to local modular change in fins/jaws. The thesis as a universal claim is therefore REFUTED in its strong form and SUPPORTED in a bounded (taxonomic/temporal horizon) form. Remaining: the non-fish, non-arthropod figure pairs (T1917-053..061).
pass2.method: Per-pair low-parameter warp vs similarity/affine/box nulls, LOO-CV, noise-floor criterion (repo standard).
pass2.blockers: None for the synthesis row (roll-up of descendants)

claims.claim: Human (and animal) heads/faces and proportions, in the Durer/Camper tradition, are mutually transformable by coordinate deformation; differences of facial angle/proportion are whole-grid deformations.

pass2.what_remains: RESOLVED 2026-10-30 (overnight loop, composer-2.5, PR 315): verdict supported. His Durer-derived human proportion grids have never been landmark-tested here (the ape/human skull instance is T1917-060).
pass2.method: Landmark Durer/Thompson grids and modern head profiles; warp-family fit as per repo standard.

claims.claim: Lanceolate, ovate and cordate leaves are transforms of one another under radial (polar) coordinates about an arrest/base point; the Begonia leaf is an instance of the same radial system.

repo_evidence: thompson/run_antscan_caste_allometry_tests.py docstring formalises 'Thompson (1917, Fig. 359, p. 732) Radial-Tangential Cordate Law' and tests it on ant heads (not leaves)
pass2.what_remains: RESOLVED 2026-10-28 (overnight loop, composer-2.5, PR 299): verdict mixed. The law has been borrowed and tested on animals; Thompson's actual leaves have never been fitted. Cheap, direct, undone.
pass2.method: Fit leaf outlines (lanceolate/ovate/cordate series) with the 8p radial-cordate family vs box/affine nulls.

claims.claim: The copepods Oithona nana and Sapphirina are related by a (logarithmic/coordinate) transformation of the whole form.

repo_evidence: thompson_1917_all_arthropods_summary.json: copepods_figs_367_368 - box 4p R2 20.41%, Thompson 8p log-quad R2 84.21%, gain +63.8 pts, min Jacobian det 0.177
pass2.what_remains: Supported on Thompson's drawings (77 grid landmarks). Remains: real-specimen outlines, as was done for fish.
pass2.method: As fish: specimen photos + 600-pt outline fit.

claims.claim: The carapaces of crabs (Geryon, Corystes, Scyramathia/Rochinia, Paralomis/Lithodes, Lupa/Portunus, Chorinus etc.) are mutually transformable by rectilinear-to-curvilinear coordinate transformation.

repo_evidence: thompson_crab_carapace_audit_summary.json: on his Fig. 369 drawings, 8p Thompson R2 78.7-99.4% vs 4p box 19.4-97.1%; vs Scholtz et al. (2020) 3D-scan landmarks, Thompson 14-LM lateral-margin RMS improves accuracy 1.7-9.2x
pass2.what_remains: Supported on drawings and partly on real 3D-scan landmarks; a full 600-pt real-specimen outline test remains (the fish treatment).
pass2.method: Real carapace outlines + direct outline fitting.

claims.claim: The amphipods Harpinia, Stegocephalus and Hyperia galba form a transformation series under coordinate deformation.

pass2.what_remains: Tested on the 1917 plate within the all-arthropods audit; real-specimen outline test remains.
pass2.method: Specimen outlines as per fish/copepod rows.

claims.claim: Argyropelecus olfersii is transformed into Sternoptyx diaphana by an oblique (shear) coordinate system whose axes are inclined at 70 degrees.
claims.quote: an oblique coordinate system whose axes are inclined at an angle of 70 deg (paraphrase pinned in thompson/1917-thompson-four-families-atlas.py docstring; verify verbatim in Pass-1 extension)

repo_evidence: thompson/1917-thompson-four-families-atlas.py (Family I, 5p oblique shear; all 4,505 taxonomic + 4,334 dated pairs; exact-1917-species landmarking in datasets/thompson/thompson_1917_exact_species_landmarks.json)
pass2.what_remains: Supported as a family at intrageneric/intrafamily scale; the exact pair is landmarked from archival plates. 600-pt exact-pair outline fit is the remaining upgrade.
pass2.method: Direct outline fitting on the exact pair (repo silhouette pipeline).

claims.claim: Deforming the rectilinear coordinates of a typical Scarus into (approximately) coaxial circles gives 'a very good outline' of Pomacanthus.
claims.quote: Fig. 375 is an outline diagram of a typical Scaroid fish. Let us deform its rectilinear co-ordinates into a system of (approximately) coaxial circles, as in Fig. 376, and then filling into the new system, space by space and point by point, our former diagram of Scarus, we obtain a very good outline of an allied fish, belonging to a neighbouring family, of the genus Pomacanthus. (Thompson 1917, p. 749; quoted verbatim in thompson/1917-thompson-scarus-pomacanthus.py L5-13)

pass2.what_remains: REFUTED in its literal (conformal/Mobius) reading: Mobius explains 0.8-1% (a conformal map cannot change depth/length 0.377->0.587); the generous oblique-coaxial reading explains 32% at genus-mean landmarks (31st percentile of all genus pairs), LOO-CV fails (0.0371 > 0.0312), and on real outlines every deformation is WORSE than no deformation (IoU 0.618 coaxial vs 0.662 similarity). Remediation already listed in the audit: digitise his drawn grid, fit maps to outlines directly, more individuals.
pass2.method: Audit remediation items 1-3 (grid digitisation, outline-fitted maps, multi-individual).
